question: How to download capital gains statement?
answer: To download your Capital Gains Statement for HDFC Mutual Funds: (1) HDFC MF Portal: Go to the official HDFC Mutual Fund Request Statement page, select 'Capital Gains Statement', enter your PAN or Folio Number, and choose the financial year to receive it via email. (2) CAMS Online: Visit the CAMS Investor Services Portal (camsonline.com) > Statements > Capital Gain / Gain Loss Statement, enter your registered email ID, and select the required financial year. (3) Investment Apps: If purchased via Groww, Zerodha, Kuvera, or Paytm Money, navigate to Profile/Reports > Tax Reports/Capital Gains in your respective app.

question: How to download account statement?
answer: To download your HDFC Mutual Fund account statement: (1) HDFC MF Portal: Visit the HDFC MF Request Statement Portal, select 'Account Statement', enter your PAN or Folio Number, and select the financial year. (2) CAMS Online: Visit camsonline.com > Statements > Account Statement, enter your registered email ID. (3) Investment Apps: Check the Reports or Statements section in Groww, Zerodha, Kuvera, or Paytm Money.

question: What is the minimum SIP amount?
answer: Minimum SIP amounts vary by scheme. HDFC Large Cap Fund: ₹100, HDFC ELSS Tax Saver: ₹500, HDFC Small Cap Fund: ₹100, HDFC Balanced Advantage Fund: ₹100, HDFC Mid Cap Fund: ₹100. Please check the specific scheme page for the most current minimum.

question: What is the lock-in period for ELSS funds?
answer: All ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Scheme) funds have a mandatory 3-year lock-in period from the date of unit allocation under Section 80C. Each SIP installment is locked in for 3 years from its respective investment date. There is no exit load after the 3-year lock-in period completes.

question: What is the exit load?
answer: Exit load varies by scheme. HDFC Large Cap Fund: 1% if redeemed within 1 year. HDFC ELSS Tax Saver: Nil (after 3-year lock-in). HDFC Small Cap Fund: 1% if redeemed within 1 year. HDFC Balanced Advantage Fund: 1% if redeemed within 1 year. HDFC Mid Cap Fund: 1% if redeemed within 1 year.

question: How are mutual fund returns taxed?
answer: Mutual fund taxation in India depends on the type of fund (equity vs. non-equity) and the holding period: 1. Equity Mutual Funds (≥ 65% in Indian equities): Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG): Applies to units held for 12 months or less. Taxed at 20%. Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG): Applies to units held for more than 12 months. Gains up to ₹1.25 lakh per financial year are tax-exempt; gains exceeding ₹1.25 lakh are taxed at 12.5% (without indexation benefits). 2. Debt & Non-Equity Mutual Funds: Specified Mutual Funds (≤ 35% equity exposure): Gains are treated as Short-Term Capital Gains regardless of holding duration and are added to your total income and taxed at your applicable income tax slab rate. Other Non-Equity Funds (35% to 65% equity, e.g., certain hybrid/gold funds): Held ≤ 24 months: Taxed at your income tax slab rate. Held > 24 months: Taxed at 12.5% without indexation. 3. Dividends (IDCW Option): Dividends received from any mutual fund scheme are added to your overall income and taxed according to your income tax slab rate. Additionally, Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) at 10% applies if dividend payouts exceed ₹5,000 in a financial year.

question: What is the tax on equity mutual funds?
answer: Equity Mutual Funds (≥ 65% in Indian equities): Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) - units held for 12 months or less are taxed at 20%. Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) - units held for more than 12 months: gains up to ₹1.25 lakh per financial year are tax-exempt; gains exceeding ₹1.25 lakh are taxed at 12.5% without indexation benefits.

question: What is the tax on debt mutual funds?
answer: Debt Mutual Funds: Investments made on or after April 1, 2023: All capital gains (irrespective of holding period) are treated as STCG and added to your total income, taxed at your applicable income tax slab rate. Investments made before April 1, 2023: If held for more than 36 months, gains qualify as LTCG and are taxed at 20% with indexation benefit.

question: What is the tax on hybrid mutual funds?
answer: Hybrid Funds: Equity-Oriented Hybrid Funds (≥ 65% equity) are taxed like equity mutual funds (20% STCG / 12.5% LTCG). Debt-Oriented Hybrid Funds (< 35% equity, purchased post-April 2023) are taxed as per your income tax slab rate.

question: How are mutual fund dividends taxed?
answer: Dividends (IDCW Option): Dividends received from any mutual fund scheme are added to your total income and taxed at your applicable income tax slab rate. Additionally, Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) at 10% applies if total dividend income from a mutual fund house exceeds ₹5,000 in a financial year.

question: What is short-term capital gains tax on mutual funds?
answer: Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) on Equity Mutual Funds: Units held for 12 months or less are taxed at 20%. For Debt Mutual Funds: All gains are treated as STCG and taxed at your applicable income tax slab rate.

question: What is long-term capital gains tax on mutual funds?
answer: Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on Equity Mutual Funds: Units held for more than 12 months. Gains up to ₹1.25 lakh per financial year are tax-exempt; gains exceeding ₹1.25 lakh are taxed at 12.5% without indexation benefits.
